industry.why: Neutral, carried, with the evidence moved towards the tape. Component 1 regime, 30-Oct-26 (risk-off beneath a steady index, led now by credit and the cost of debt rather than by the artificial intelligence wash-out alone: the US ten-year above 5% after a hawkish Fed hold with two dissents for a hike, Goldman Sachs' Risk Appetite Indicator at its lowest since April 2025, euro investment-grade and high-yield yields up 30 and 90 basis points since September, Brent near $115, the French premium a record 150 basis points, Europe rotating to quality, defensives and non-AI growth, the STOXX Europe 600 1.7% from its high with breadth recovering from the bottom fifth of three years and defensives leading cyclicals at four weeks and three months; sources present 2026-W44): third-quarter beats were sold (Sandvik down 5%, Atlas Copco down 8%, Hiab down 12%), Danske Bank's C-J (25 October) says 'a lot is priced in' with the order strength coming from data centres the market no longer pays for, and the exception is the non-AI compounder (Hexagon, 13% organic growth); against it, offshore services and nuclear have multi-year visibility and electrical equipment is still the physical bottleneck. Relative strength per 31-relative-strength.md, 2026-10-30 against 2026-08-28, not week on week: D now, C prior. The sector rows do the work: Electrical equipment, Diversified groups, Distributors, Test and measurement and Engineered components at C, Flow control and Building technology at D. Five live holdings (19.35 points of the book) sit here, judged in component 4. Counter-case for D: a tape that sells beats is a regime statement; for B: the order data remain the strongest non-AI demand read in the pack. To D on a second week of beats sold with relative strength falling to F.

sector.key: O.18. Test, measurement, sensing and safety technology
sector.why: Neutral, set deliberately this week (carried C). Component 1 regime, 16-Oct-26 (a discount-rate shock with the first credit crack inside the artificial intelligence chain: United States core inflation re-accelerating on energy, the Fed and Bank of England hikes pulled forward, the US 10-year about 5.1%, the US joined the sell-off and Asia is in washout, defensives bid for four weeks in Europe, European breadth off its three-year lows but in the bottom quarter, the consumer forecast to weaken into winter; sources present 2026-W42): regulated, recurring test and measurement demand is the proven case the regime pays for, but the group's growth leg is semiconductor and industrial capital spending, which the week de-rated; Jenoptik's memo (Mixed) states it exactly: the order book is the demand case and the 69th-percentile multiple after a doubling is the valuation case. Relative strength per 31-relative-strength.md, 2026-10-16 against 2026-08-14, not week on week: B now, C prior. Three MI Pool names (Vaisala, Jenoptik, Renishaw). Counter-case for higher: relative strength improving and Renishaw's five-of-eight A or B; for lower: the semiconductor exposure now sits under an Underweight sector. Balanced; Neutral by judgement.

geography.why: Neutral, carried, with the evidence for Underweight named and judged thin. Goldman Sachs (16 Oct) names 'worrying debt dynamics' in Finland alongside France, Belgium, Austria and Finland; that is one clause in one note with no spread reading, the same footing on which Ireland was held Neutral last week for Overweight, so the row does not move on it. Component 1 regime, 23-Oct-26 (risk-off confirmed and broadening: the discount-rate squeeze now a positioning wash-out in the artificial intelligence complex with credit leading it, bonds rallied as a hedge for the first time this cycle while the Fed still hikes in December, the US 10-year near 5.10%, Brent $111, French sovereign stress spilling into Italy, European defensives leading cyclicals on all five windows and breadth in the bottom fifth of three years; sources present 2026-W43). Relative strength is not graded by country. Moves to D if a second source names Finland or a spread reading is read widening.
